newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lufthansa partner sees May end to fuel surcharge.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa partner sees May end to fuel surcharge.

text.p: Lufthansa Cargo AG may drop its fuel surcharge in early May, a Frankfurt-based United Airlines official forecast.

The Germany cargo sales manager for UAL -- a Lufthansa partner airline -- Robert Blythe told Reuters the recent decision by Delta Air Lines to drop its 10 U.S. cents per kg surcharge from March 13 had put other airlines under pressure.
"I think Lufthansa will go on May 1 and after that it is a question of time when the others follow. That is my guess," he said.
Lufthansa Cargo spokesman Dietrich Seidl said earlier today that the German freight airline, which was the first to impose a surcharge last November, saw no reason at present to make any change.
"We are remaining by our statement that the fuel surcharge will be kept until the jet fuel prices have reached the level of last July," he stressed.
Blythe added: "But the problem is what happens if the prices go up again. Will Delta put the surcharge back on again?" he added.
United would try to keep a surcharge on as long as possible, he said.
Konrad Bossdorf, Air Canada cargo manager Germany, criticised Delta's decision to drop the surcharge with immediate effect.
"Fuel prices have only gone down a few cents but are not down to the levels of last June," he said.
"I think there is no need to cut the surcharge," he added.
